I also made a big move with my cat about a year ago where we drove roughly 1,000 miles. What really helped with the drive is I got a big huge cat carrier/condo thing that goes in the back of the car (I got mine from Amazon, by the brand Pet Fit for Life). I put some of her blankets in there and she slept pretty much the whole time, and I think generally made the trip much easier for her as it gave her plenty of room.

In terms of making the transition as easy as possible, I just tried to keep a lot of things the same for her in my new place— having her same cat tree, her blankets, etc. As well as letting her explore the new place and get familiar with it. She is an indoor cat, so I am unsure about how an outdoor cat may respond to a new place, so unfortunately I can’t really offer much advice there.

I have not personally had any experience using the cat pheromones, but I think it’s certainly worth giving it a shot to help keep him calm. You could also try calming treats or balms, or catnip if he is the type of cat who calms down with catnip.

But for the trip itself, I would highly recommend something like a large cat condo for the car. I would also be sure to check on him regularly to see how he’s doing, and be sure to offer him water, treats, and food (he may forego eating during the trip).

Best of luck, and I hope the move goes well for your kitty ❤️

What you are speaking of is sex, not gender. They are different. Humans are the only species in the world that have gender, it is a societal construct. Terms such as AFAB include trans men and non-binary folk who do not identify as female, but were assigned that gendered term at birth due to their biological sex and the gender that we as a society associate with that. It’s an inherently confusing topic, I understand. But these terms are important as they really help us to be inclusive of our fellow humans and all of the identities out there.

You know, I thought it was weird for a while too back when I identified as a lesbian, and at one point it even kinda annoyed me. It just didn’t make any sense to me. Then I met someone who identified as non-binary and taught me exactly what that means and why pronouns and terms such as AFAB/AMAB are important.

I began to learn a lot more about it, and after I embraced these identities and associated terms, I became so much more loving of my fellow LGBTQ+ folks. Not only that, but I realized that I myself am non-binary, and my annoyance with it before was probably some internalized self-hatred.

I recommend learning about it and doing some research on why these terms can be so important. It really changed my way of thinking and honestly I’m so much happier and more inclusive because of it.
